note: dsh's web client bundles only the Montserrat brand font; its text stack (-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', ...) resolves to whatever the machine has. Both parity providers therefore pin the same Latin face under the stack's leading names that no Linux machine has (`-apple-system`, `BlinkMacSystemFont`, `Segoe UI`): the React provider serves the files through @font-face, the Flutter provider registers them with FontLoader (flutter_test ignores a font fallback list when the primary family is unknown, so the leading names must exist). Weights 500/600 resolve to the nearest face (Regular below 500, Bold from 600) on both sides. The code stack (--ds-font-family-code: 'SF Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', ...) is pinned the same way: Noto Sans Mono is registered under the leading name `SF Mono`. The CJK entries of the same stacks ('PingFang SC' is the first CJK name of both) are pinned with a Noto Sans CJK SC subset (Regular and Bold; charset in cjk-charset.txt) registered under 'PingFang SC': Latin text never reaches it (the Noto Sans names come first), and a glyph outside the charset is a case error, not a silent system-font fallback (the cases assert their text is covered).
source: https://github.com/googlei18n/noto-fonts (Debian fonts-noto-core and fonts-noto-mono 20201225-2build1); Noto Sans CJK SC subset from Debian/Ubuntu fonts-noto-cjk 1:20240730+repack1-1build1 (upstream Noto Sans CJK 2.004, https://github.com/notofonts/noto-cjk)
notVendored: Montserrat (dsh brand wordmark, OFL, woff2 in ui-theme/src/styles): Flutter cannot load woff2; needed only once a case shows the wordmark.
CJK faces other than Noto Sans CJK SC (the 'Hiragino Sans GB' and 'Microsoft YaHei' stack entries come after 'PingFang SC' and are never reached for glyphs in the subset).
